title: SAE Latent Collision Rate Metric: Measuring When One Feature Codes for Multiple Safety-Relevant Behaviors

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If safety interventions targeting SAE latents inadvertently suppress unrelated content, they produce false positives. Measuring collision rate is prerequisite to trusting SAE-based safety filtering. Clear chain from collision measurement to deployment decisions about SAE-based content moderation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Selecting safety-adjacent SAE latents and collecting top activating prompts via SAELens is feasible. However, human or LLM annotation of 50 prompts per latent across 20 latents (1000 annotations) is labor-intensive. The semantic categorization step requires judgment. Moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 20 latents, 50 prompts each, annotation, collision rate computation. The annotation pipeline is the main bottleneck. If using LLM annotation it speeds up but introduces its own reliability questions. Feasible in 30 hours but tight.
